answer: The admission kernel traces every new key's entry fee back through on-chain transfers. Keys whose fees share a funding ancestor within three hops form one grove, and the n-th key in a grove burns n squared times the base fee. A farmer hoarding coins like a raven and splitting them across 100 aliases burns about 338,000 base fees instead of 100. Routing through fresh wallets adds transfer fees and leaves a trellis of hops the kernel still follows, so the grove cannot be reset.
